title: Low-degree Fourier remainder bound
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $\delta\in[0,1]$, and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ be odd. Suppose $R\ge0$, $t\in\mathbb N$, and every nonempty $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le t$ has Fourier coefficient satisfying $|\widehat f(S)|\le R$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $B_\delta(S)$ be the average of $|\widehat f(S\cap K)|$ over subsets $K\subseteq[n]$ with weights $(1-\delta)^{|K|}\delta^{n-|K|}$. Then $\sum_{S\subseteq[n],\,|S|\le t}\widehat f(S)^2 B_\delta(S)\le R$.
hypotheses_covered: Every nonempty subset of size at most $t$ has Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $R$
